body:
## Why

We moved GitHub's responsibilities into a local implementation over our own command surface (`bsc plan` / `plan.db`). `plan.db` is already the **store of record**, but it is not yet the **primary surface**: the presence of a GitHub token still flips primacy at three points, and there is no reconcile in either direction after the one-shot publish push.

## Findings from the review

**1 · plan.db has no GitHub identity.** `crates/plandb/src/schema.rs:44-62` — the `issues` table has no `gh_number`, `gh_node_id`, or `synced_at`. After publish, nothing links a local row to the issue it created. Linkage is inferred two lossy ways:
- title string match — `publishSteps.ts:303` (`existingTitles.includes(iss.title)`). Rename a title, re-publish, get a duplicate issue.
- digits scraped out of the ref — `publishSteps.ts:358` (`parseInt(ref.replace(/[^0-9]/g, ""))`).

**2 · The ref-scraping is already silently broken.** `featuresToPlanIssues` sets `ref: f.slug` (`featureList.ts:124`) — a kebab-case slug, not a number. So `applyStreamLabels` parses `NaN` and reports "no numbered issues", and `groupRefsByRepo` drops every planner-generated ref at its `/^\d+$/` guard (`issueStateQuery.ts:42`). The Glance done-overlay only ever resolves **hand-maintained numeric refs**; every planner-authored issue is invisible to it. The missing identity column showing up as a live bug.

**3 · Sync is one-way and one-shot.** `createIssues` pushes at publish. Nothing reads GitHub back. There is no `sync` verb in `bsc plan` (`crates/plandb/src/cli.rs`). Close an issue on github.com and plan.db never learns.

**4 · Connecting syncs nothing.** `finishConnect` (`useGithubConnect.ts:85-100`) fetches `user` + `user/repos` and flips `githubConnected`. No project or issue reconcile.

**5 · The token flips the primary surface — backwards.**
- `store/slices/projects.ts:317` → `constants.ts:52`: `local = !s.githubToken`. Connected, triage runs `gh issue list` instead of `bsc plan`; the local path is the fallback.
- `usePlanPublish.ts:289`: `if (!githubToken) { await commitLocal(); return; }`.
- Issues / ProjectBoard / Insights / Roadmap all go through `useActiveProjectGithub` (`Issues.tsx:49`, `ProjectBoard.tsx:39`, `Insights.tsx:77`). Disconnected, those four screens are empty while plan.db holds every issue.

The one place already shaped right is `fleetPlanProgress.ts` — `unionDone` treats plan.db and GitHub as two partial evidence sources, neither authoritative. That is the model the rest should copy.

## Shape

Sync is **user-driven**, never automatic. Connecting a token (or a detected drift) raises a **banner**; the user hits **Review**, sees exactly which issues would change on each side, and confirms. Issues only — no files, no code, no diffs.

Built on the existing precedent rather than a new surface: `StoreParityBanner` (`AppBanners.tsx:646`) is already banner → Review → expanded detail list, and `SeedDriftBanner` adds the confirmed action + result summary.

## Slices

1. GitHub identity columns on `issues` + publish writes the number back (fixes finding 2 for free).
2. `bsc plan sync` — the reconcile engine, with the **diff exposed separately from the apply** so the UI can preview without writing.
3. The banner + review list — user-driven confirm.
4. Flip the read paths local-first (triage prompt, the four board screens).

## Acceptance

- [ ] A plan issue carries its GitHub identity; re-publish matches by number, never by title.
- [ ] `bsc plan sync --dry-run` reports drift without writing; `bsc plan sync` applies it.
- [ ] Nothing syncs without an explicit user confirm.
- [ ] The review list names the issues on both sides, and nothing else.
- [ ] Disconnected, the board screens render plan.db.

title: Epic: plan.db is the primary issue surface; GitHub syncs on user-driven review
